thread:
ops-bot: ALERT — p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming-continuous-batching (us-west-2).
ops-bot: Rule: service="inference-stream" env="prod" path="/v1/stream" metric=p99_latency > 5s for 3m. Auto-page: #eng-oncall.

alice.chen: seeing the same in dashboards — p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 =~ 6.8s, error rate low but a lot of streaming stalls (streaming stalls metric up x6). Correlates with cont-batch pack growth on hosts pool-c.

mateo.rivera: joining. Any recent deploys to streaming-batcher or scheduler? I see a canary yesterday touching pack-shed heuristics.

priya.singh: no deploys in the last 6h from our side. We did enable a change to default pack_high_water=0.85 earlier this week (eng-infra). Could be amplification with mixed sequence lengths.

jordan.oncall: quick customer impact: 3 tenants (ten-svc-7, ten-svc-8, ten-svc-23) show increased request latencies — approx 0.7% of global traffic hitting >5s. CX ping in flight. @sam.cx FYI.

sam.cx: got it — I'll draft an interim customer note if this persists >30m. Which mitigation are we trying first?

alice.chen: mitigation plan proposal (fastest, low risk):
1) Disable continuous batching for streaming route (runtime flag) -> route streaming -> fallback to immediate streaming path (no contpack).
2) Apply temporary pack_shed hard-cap to 8 on pool-c to avoid large pack formation.
3) Route small sequences to fast streaming variant (model-small) for 10% traffic via canary.

mateo.rivera: agree. How do we flip cont-batch off quickly? Is there a runtime toggle? Eng-infra, can you confirm command?

eng-infra-bot: runtime flag available: `--enable_continuous_batching` (service config). To disable without deploy, set feature flag in configstore: `features/contbatch/enable=false` and signal workers to reload config. Patch takes ~30-60s to propagate.

alice.chen: steps I'm doing now:
- PATCH configstore:
```
PATCH /api/v1/config/features/contbatch
{ "enable": false, "reason": "p99 spike live mitigation" }
```
- curl health endpoints to ensure reloads
```
for host in $(cat affected_hosts.txt); do curl -s http://$host:8080/metrics | grep CONTBATCH || echo $host; done
```

priya.singh: also applying pack cap via scheduler API:
```
POST /api/v1/scheduler/pool-c/pack_caps
{ "max_pack_size": 8 }
```

hannah.sre: running the rollout with careful monitoring — will keep auto-scaling enabled. I'll watch p99 and streaming_stalls metrics.

ops-bot: (metric snapshot) p95: 1.12s, p99: 6.79s, streaming_stalls: +520% vs baseline, in-flight requests approx 12k.

mateo.rivera: after disabling contbatch on pool-c (started now). Observed immediate drop in pack size distribution — median pack size down from 18 -> 4 on sampled nodes.

alice.chen: good sign. Early telemetry: tail latency dropping — p99 went from 6.8s -> 3.9s in 45s after change. Still above SLO but improving.

priya.singh: running a sampling job to identify request seqlen distribution that caused amplification:
```
SELECT seq_len_bucket, count(*) FROM stream_requests WHERE host IN (pool-c) AND ts > now() - 10m GROUP BY seq_len_bucket
```
Result: heavy mode at 4-8 tokens but a long-tail at 1024+ causing KV cache pressure and slow pack flush.

jordan.oncall: customer impact update: ten-svc-23 shows retries & user-visible timeouts on long chat streams. Sam, we should let them know we have mitigation in progress and expected stabilization in ~15-30m.

sam.cx: will send note with current mitigations and ETA 30m. I'll include temporary workaround: reduce request concurrency client-side if possible.

hannah.sre: monitoring loop: alert if p99 > 5s for 10m post-mitigation, and if streaming_stalls > 200% for 5m. Also watching host CPU (pack building is CPU-heavy), KV cache evictions.

eng-infra-bot: additional mitigation available: temporarily increase kv-cache TTL to reduce eviction churn (configstore flag `kvcache/ttl`), but that may increase memory pressure. Use only if pack cap + contbatch off insufficient.

mateo.rivera: agree prefer pack cap + contbatch off first. If tail persists, consider kvcache TTL tweak + reduce max_concurrent_packs to 2 on the worst hosts.

alice.chen: recorded quick playbook entries in thread for next on-call:
- timeline of actions and times
- commands used
- customer impact summary
- link to grafana panels

alice.chen: handoff note for next rotation (copy below):
- Incident root cause: cont-batch pack amplification under mixed sequence-length workload created large packs and KV cache churn causing streaming stalls and p99 tail spikes.
- Mitigations performed: disabled cont-batch for streaming route (features/contbatch/enable=false), set scheduler pool-c max_pack_size=8, canaried model-small for 10% traffic, monitoring in place.
- Current status: p99 reduced from 6.8s -> 2.4s over 15min, streaming_stalls trending down. Customer retries decreasing.
- Next actions for on-call: decide long-term fix (pack heuristics tune vs. contbatch adaptive cap), coordinate with product to notify impacted customers, schedule follow-up postmortem if incident persists >24h.

jordan.oncall: adding that we should run synthetic replay for mixed seqlen to validate heuristics before re-enabling contbatch.

priya.singh: will own the replay job and a proposed scheduler tweak (adaptive pack cap based on seqlen variance).

mateo.rivera: thumbs — will draft patch to pack-shed heuristic: consider weighted seqlen mean and cap pack formation when variance > threshold.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. Will auto-close page when p99 < 2.5s for 20m and streaming_stalls < 120%.

hannah.sre: leaving a final note here for handoff: please escalate to infra if pack size re-amplifies after re-enable. Saved logs & traces under /incidents/3478912345/. Contact: alice.chen, mateo.rivera.

sam.cx: customer note sent.

alice.chen: thanks all — marking thread for post-incident writeup. Moving to monitor mode; ping @oncall if regressions.
